echelon_key.poi: Front Line Medic/CCP (point of injury / combat casualty care)

extraction_notes: Each physical card prints ONE vitals progression (poi -> role1 -> role2), not separate branching tables. Some cells carry an inline '(if treated)' qualifier.

Cells marked inferred:true are NOT printed on the card — they're clinically plausible values or branch logic I generated to satisfy the state-machine/rules requirement, per your instructions to flag anything invented.
'XXXX' on the card (value unobtainable at that echelon) is stored as null.
Card image/photo on the front is not reproduced (copyrighted training-aid artwork); only text fields are extracted.
Cards 45-47 (Expectant/Poly Trauma) use POI/Role I/Role II headers abbreviated as "POI" rather than the usual "Front Line Medic/CCP" wording, but otherwise have a standard vitals table.

Card 48 (KIA) uses different echelon labels on its back page ("Front Line Medic/CCP" / "Unit Collection Point" / "MACP/BSA") still mapped to poi/role1/role2; all three echelons print an identical flatline presentation.

Card 49 (Safety/ROE) has no vitals table at all on either side -- its front prints explicit OC/T branching instructions (evac category depends on whether safety equipment was provided/used/available) which are modeled as rules with an "evac_override"/"triage_override" field the app applies when that action is logged; states are a single qualitative "baseline".
A few cards print the literal word "Unknown" for a vital (distinct from the deck's usual "XXXX" unobtainable marker) -- stored as the string "Unknown", not null, to preserve that distinction.

Every action id referenced in a card's rules is guaranteed to exist as a button in app/src/interventions.js (run data/validate.mjs after any hand-edit to re-check this and other structural invariants).

player_tracking.note: The physical card's blank admin fields (Battle Roster #, Unit, OCT Call Sign/P2P, POI DTG, and the OCT STATUS/GIVEN WIA-DOW-RTD box) are runtime data filled in during an exercise, not static per-card facts — so they live under each card's 'admin_template' as the blank shape the app instantiates per session, and the actual filled-in values go in the app's session ledger (localStorage), one instance per scan/patient run, keyed by battle_roster + card id + session start time. This lets the same physical card be reused across multiple trainees/exercises without collision.

untreated.note: PERRL/mental status row prints 'L Eye Normal' at every echelon since the right eye is the injured/affected eye and cannot be meaningfully assessed for pupil reactivity.

treated.note: Rigid eye shield placed over the injured globe (no pressure/patch directly on the eye). Does not change these measured vitals; the effect is prevention of further mechanical injury to the globe.

deteriorating.note: Not a vital-sign-driven deterioration — systemic vitals stay essentially normal. If a rigid shield is not applied (or pressure/patching is placed directly on the globe) and the eye is bumped or rubbed, a penetrating globe injury risks extruding intraocular contents and permanent vision loss. Vitals reused from untreated since this is a local/functional complication, not a hemodynamic one.
